$comment: TELEMETRY: every full-rate GT7 frame, from every source (live, replay-<run>, parity), kept as a flight recorder so logbook can pick a lap up again after a restart (ADR 0001, point 1; paddock#36). The store, not this stream, is the record.
subjects: twr.v1.*.frame.gt7 only. The single * is the source token, so the 20 Hz copy twr.v1.<src>.frame.gt7.lo (one token longer) is not captured.
max_age 2 h (7200000000000 ns): ADR 0001's starting value, long enough to cover a logbook restart mid-session.

max_bytes 2 GiB (2147483648): ADR 0001 puts a frame as JSON at about 1.3 KB, 60 a second, about 280 MB an hour; the full CloudEvents headers (paddock#34) add about 43 MB an hour, so about 325 MB an hour. 2 h of live is about 650 MB. A replay at --speed max writes an hour of frames in seconds, and discard old would push live frames out first, so the limit is about 6 h of frames: 2 h of live with room for replays (paddock#36, decision of 2026-10-24).
discard old: a full stream drops its oldest frames, never refuses new ones, so the frame path never sees an error.

duplicate_window 2 min (120000000000 ns): frames carry Nats-Msg-Id <run>:frame:<seq> (paddock#34), so a frame ecu publishes twice after a reconnect is stored once. Live, at 60 Hz, that is about 7,200 ids held. A replay at --speed max publishes far faster, so it holds far more: every frame of a 1 h recording, about 216,000 ids, a few tens of MB of server memory for 2 min, which is acceptable.
max_msg_size -1: bounded by the server's max_payload (1 MiB by default), far above a frame. max_msgs, max_msgs_per_subject and max_consumers -1: max_bytes and max_age are the limits.
num_replicas 1: one NATS server (ADR 0004). File storage so a server restart keeps the frames.
name: TELEMETRY
description: Full-rate frames from every source, a 2 h flight recorder for logbook (paddock#36).
